🇺🇸 AMERICA.GOV IS COMING — AND THE DOGE CONNECTION IS HARD TO MISS

The Trump administration is preparing to unveil America.gov on Tuesday, September 29 — a new AI-powered portal designed to become a centralized “front door” for interacting with the federal government.

And this could be much bigger than just another government website.

The reported vision includes:

🤖 AI-FIRST GOVERNMENT — Instead of figuring out which agency or website you need, an AI assistant could help direct you to the appropriate federal service.

🛂 PASSPORT SERVICES — Passport applications and renewals are reportedly among the services being targeted for integration.

💰 DIRECT TAX FILING — Officials have reportedly explored allowing Americans with relatively simple returns to file their federal taxes directly through the system for free.

🪪 ONE DIGITAL IDENTITY — Integration with Login.gov has been discussed, potentially allowing one verified identity to access multiple federal services.

🏛️ CENTRALIZING GOVERNMENT SERVICES — Rather than navigating dozens of disconnected federal websites, America.gov could eventually provide a single interface connecting citizens to numerous agencies.

And here's where it gets especially interesting:

This project has major DOGE fingerprints on it.

The effort is being driven by the White House National Design Studio, headed by Airbnb co-founder and former DOGE figure Joe Gebbia, while other former DOGE personnel have reportedly been involved in the broader modernization effort.

And Elon Musk himself is expected to attend the unveiling Tuesday, along with Trump, JD Vance, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and other major technology leaders.

To be precise: America.gov isn't “Elon's website.” But there is a clear lineage running from the DOGE government-modernization project into what is now being built.

The real question is what America.gov ultimately becomes.

If this evolves into AI + Login.gov + taxes + passports + federal services all operating through one unified portal, we're potentially looking at something much larger than a website redesign.

We're looking at an attempt to rebuild the interface between the American people and the federal government itself.

Tuesday's unveiling should tell us just how far along that transformation really is.

🇺🇸🇷🇺 US and Russia strip AI safeguards from UN autonomous weapons text – Washington Post

The US and Russia pushed through the removal of key restrictions on the military use of AI from a UN draft on lethal autonomous weapons, The Washington Post reports, citing negotiation participants and documents it reviewed.

At the Geneva talks, the delegations reportedly removed:

➡️the requirement that a human review AI-selected targets before a strike;

➡️provisions requiring ethical considerations;

➡️language requiring such systems to operate "predictably" and "reliably."

According to WaPo, on the final day of talks the American and Russian delegations spent about 15 hours reworking the document. Each fielded a team of roughly ten lawyers, almost twice the size of other delegations.

The talks are part of a UN effort to set international rules for lethal autonomous systems that can select and engage targets on their own. The agreed text is non-binding. Countries will meet again in Geneva in November to decide whether to open negotiations on a full international treaty. More than 70 states back the text as a basis for binding rules, but the process runs on consensus. Washington and Moscow both oppose legally binding limits, so they can effectively block it.

The technology is already in use. In March, WaPo reported that the US military relied on Anthropic's Claude, integrated into Palantir's Maven Smart System, to suggest and prioritize targets and generate coordinates as it struck around 1,000 targets in the first 24 hours of the war on Iran.
